LESSON: MASS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.2: Mass
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mass, part of Measurement in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can you measure mass of materials? 2. Why do we determine the mass of objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mass together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner role plays addition of mass in kilograms using items in the classroom model shop.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: learner makes masses of 1kg using sand or soil by measuring against the kilogram

standard unit.

Values:
● Respect: learner shares experiences on measuring mass of different objects.

● Unity: learner shares resources amicably as they make masses of objects to use in learning.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Safety: learner safely collects materials needed for learning from their immediate environment.

28

Link to other learning areas:

● The learner is able to relate skills used in preparing mass of different object to moulding in Creative Activities.

Learning resources:

Masses of 1kg, soil, sand, beam balance, digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, screen magnifiers

and tactile keyboards.
